etymology: From Ancient Greek en- (in) + trope (transformation, turning). Coined by Rudolf Clausius in 1865.

definitions.physics: A thermodynamic state function (S) representing the unavailable thermal energy per unit temperature (dS = dQ_rev / T), fundamentally quantifying the logarithmic measure of microstates corresponding to a macroscopic state (S = k_B * ln W).
definitions.general: A measure of disorder, randomness, or uncertainty in a physical or informational system.

example_sentence: According to the Second Law of Thermodynamics, the total entropy of an isolated system always increases over time.

etymology: From Greek phos (light) + synthesis (putting together, combination).

definitions.botany: The anabolic biochemical pathway wherein chlorophyll pigments in thylakoid membranes transduce solar photons (400-700nm) into chemical energy, photolyzing water into O2 and fixing atmospheric CO2 into hexose carbohydrates via the Calvin-Benson cycle.
definitions.general: The natural process by which green plants and certain organisms synthesize nutrients using sunlight.

multilingual_translations.hi: प्रकाश-संश्लेषण (पौधों द्वारा भोजन निर्माण की प्रक्रिया)

example_sentence: Photosynthesis produces the primary biomass of Earth's terrestrial and marine trophic pyramids.

faculty: Faculty of Law, Governance & Constitutional Jurisprudence
etymology: From Latin constitutio (an establishment, decree, statute), from constituere (to cause to stand, set up).

definitions.law: The foundational supreme legal charter of a sovereign state, institutionalizing the separation of powers (Legislature, Executive, Judiciary), establishing rule of law, and codifying inviolable fundamental rights for citizens.
definitions.general: The composition or physical makeup of something; or the basic principles by which an organization is governed.

example_sentence: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the land, prevailing over all conflicting statutory enactments.

etymology: From Greek pathos (suffering, disease) + -genes (producer of, born of).

definitions.pathology: Any biological microorganism (fungus, bacterium, virus, viroid, oomycete, phytoplasma, or nematode) capable of disrupting the normal physiological functioning of a host organism and inducing clinical disease symptoms.
definitions.general: An infectious biological agent that causes illness or disease.

example_sentence: Phytophthora infestans is an aggressive oomycete pathogen responsible for devastating potato late blight epidemics.

faculty: Faculty of Botanical Sciences & Plant Physiology
etymology: From Latin trans (across, through) + spirare (to breathe).

definitions.botany: The physiological vaporization of water from plant aerial surfaces, predominantly through stomatal pores in leaf mesophyll, generating negative hydrostatic tension that drives xylem sap ascent from root systems.
definitions.general: The release of moisture vapor through pores in an organism.

example_sentence: Transpiration provides essential evaporative cooling that protects the photosystem complexes of plant leaves during peak midday heat flux.

etymology: From Latin juris prudentia (the science or skill of law), from jus (right, law) + prudentia (knowledge, foresight).

definitions.law: The theoretical philosophy, science, and structural analysis of law and legal principles, examining the origins, authority, and normative justifications of judicial systems.
definitions.general: A particular legal department, judicial philosophy, or body of court rulings.

multilingual_translations.hi: विधिशास्त्र (कानून का वैज्ञानिक व दार्शनिक अध्ययन)

example_sentence: Modern constitutional jurisprudence relies on the doctrine of proportionality to balance individual liberties against executive restrictions.
